subject: Business Models
title: AI as a Service
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: AI as a Service.

hook.text: OpenAI charges $0.002 per 1,000 tokens. Intelligence itself is now a metered utility you pay per use.

buildup.text: AI-as-a-Service lets any company add intelligence to their products via API calls billed by consumption.

discovery.text: This model democratizes AI. A 2-person startup and a Fortune 500 company access the same GPT-4 model.

twist.text: Dependence on AI providers creates risk. If OpenAI changes pricing or policies, thousands of businesses are affected.

climax.text: AI-as-a-Service is the fastest-growing business model in tech history. It's reshaping every industry simultaneously.

punchline.text: $0.002 per 1,000 tokens. Intelligence is now a metered utility.

quiz.question: What does AI-as-a-Service democratize?
options: Access to advanced AI capabilities via API

details.summary: AI-as-a-service provides artificial intelligence capabilities through cloud APIs, allowing companies to add machine learning features without building models from scratch..
details.whyItMatters: AIaaS democratizes access to AI capabilities that previously required massive datasets and specialized teams. It is creating a new platform layer in technology infrastructure with implications as significant as cloud computing's disruption of.
takeaways: Cloud APIs deliver pre-trained AI models for language, vision, and prediction
Pay-per-use pricing makes AI accessible without upfront infrastructure investment
AIaaS creates platform dependency similar to cloud infrastructure lock-in

faq.question: How does AI-as-a-service generate revenue?
faq.answer: Usage-based pricing charges per API call, per token processed, or per compute hour. Tiered subscriptions offer different capabilities and volumes. Enterprise contracts provide dedicated capacity and custom fine-tuning. Some providers offer free tiers with premium upgrades.

faq.question: What are the risks of depending on AI-as-a-service providers?
faq.answer: Vendor lock-in as applications become dependent on specific model APIs, unpredictable cost scaling with usage growth, data privacy concerns from sending sensitive data to external providers, model quality changes without warning, and competitive risk if the provider enters your market.
